vocabulary.meaning_en: what experts say the weather will be
vocabulary.example: The forecast is for rain at midday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (weather) grey and cloudy, with no sun
vocabulary.example: It's wet and dull again today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (weather) calm and not likely to change
vocabulary.example: The weather looks settled for the weekend.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (UK, informal) an umbrella
vocabulary.example: Take your brolly; it's going to rain.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (UK, informal) Wellington boots: tall rubber boots for rain and mud
vocabulary.example: It's very muddy. Put your wellies on.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (rain) falling very hard, often with wind
vocabulary.example: It's lashing outside; the umbrella is useless.

vocabulary.meaning_en: rain lightly but continuously
vocabulary.example: It's only drizzling, so we can still walk.

vocabulary.meaning_en: raining a few light drops, often at the start of rain
vocabulary.example: It's just spitting; it hasn't really started yet.

vocabulary.meaning_en: rain very heavily
vocabulary.example: It's pouring down! Stay inside.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a sudden, heavy fall of rain
vocabulary.example: We got wet in a sudden downpour.

vocabulary.meaning_en: with strong winds that change direction
vocabulary.example: It's a blustery day by the sea.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a very strong wind
vocabulary.example: There were gale-force winds last night.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a light, pleasant wind
vocabulary.example: A gentle breeze kept us cool.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a sudden, short, strong wind
vocabulary.example: A gust of wind closed the door.

vocabulary.meaning_en: extremely hot
vocabulary.example: It's boiling hot today; it's over 35 degrees.

vocabulary.meaning_en: so hot it feels like burning
vocabulary.note_en: To scorch = to burn the surface.
vocabulary.example: The sand was scorching hot.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a period of several days of very hot weather
vocabulary.example: We're in the middle of a heatwave.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a sudden, short period of very cold weather
vocabulary.example: There's a cold snap expected next week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: extremely cold
vocabulary.example: It's bitterly cold; wear a warm coat.

vocabulary.meaning_en: typical of winter: cold, with ice or snow
vocabulary.example: Drive carefully in wintry conditions.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something you say to start a conversation and help people relax
vocabulary.example: The weather is the perfect icebreaker.

fine_lines.title: It is snow ✗ vs It is snowy / It is snowing ✓
fine_lines.explanation_ar: خطأ شائع: It is snow أو It is rain. بعد It is نستخدم صفة (snowy, rainy, sunny) أو فعلًا بـ ing (snowing, raining).
fine_lines.explanation_en: A common mistake is "It is snow / It is rain". After "It is" use an adjective (snowy, rainy, sunny) or a verb in -ing (snowing, raining).

fine_lines.title: sunny / shining vs shiny
fine_lines.explanation_ar: نقول It is sunny أو The sun is shining. لا نقول It is shiny، لأن shiny تعني لامعًا (مثل سيارة نظيفة).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Say "It is sunny" or "The sun is shining". Don't say "It is shiny"; "shiny" means bright and polished, like a clean car.

fine_lines.title: Kinds of rain: spitting, drizzling, pouring, lashing
fine_lines.explanation_ar: spitting: قطرات قليلة متقطعة. drizzling: مطر خفيف مستمر. pouring down: مطر غزير جدًا. lashing: مطر غزير جدًا مع ريح.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Spitting = a few drops. Drizzling = light, continuous rain. Pouring down = very heavy rain. Lashing = very heavy rain with wind.

examples.sentence: It's spitting. Take an umbrella just in case.
It's lashing. Your umbrella will turn inside out.

fine_lines.title: breeze vs gust vs gale
fine_lines.explanation_ar: breeze: ريح خفيفة لطيفة. gust: هبّة مفاجئة قصيرة. gale: ريح قوية جدًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Breeze = light, pleasant wind. Gust = a sudden short burst. Gale = very strong wind.

examples.sentence: There's a nice breeze by the sea.
The gale blew down some trees.

expressions.example: What's it like outside? Do I need a coat?

expressions.meaning_en: A general question about the weather.
expressions.example: What's the weather like in your city?

expressions.meaning_en: Asks what the weather will be.
expressions.example: What's the weather forecast for tomorrow?

expressions.meaning_en: Asks someone who can see out of the window.
expressions.example: How's it looking outside? Is it still raining?

expressions.phrase: It looks like it always does: wet and dull.
expressions.meaning_en: A typical, slightly funny British answer.
expressions.example: What's it like out? — It looks like it always does: wet and dull.

expressions.phrase: It's not so bad today; the sun is shining.
expressions.meaning_en: Says the weather is better than usual.
expressions.example: It's not so bad today; the sun is shining.

expressions.meaning_en: A typical comment about weather forecasts.
expressions.example: I don't listen to the forecast. They always get it wrong.

expressions.phrase: It's a day for the umbrella / the brolly.
expressions.example: Look at those clouds. It's a day for the brolly.

expressions.phrase: It's a day for the wellies.
expressions.meaning_ar: إنه يوم يحتاج إلى الأحذية المطاطية.
expressions.meaning_en: Says it is very wet and muddy.
expressions.example: It's been raining all night. It's a day for the wellies.

expressions.meaning_en: Says the rain is very heavy.
expressions.example: Don't go out yet. It's pouring down.

expressions.phrase: We're in the middle of a heatwave.
expressions.meaning_en: Says it has been very hot for days.
expressions.example: We're in the middle of a heatwave. It's hard to sleep.

expressions.phrase: There's a cold snap expected next week.
expressions.meaning_ar: من المتوقع موجة برد الأسبوع القادم.
expressions.meaning_en: Says a short cold period is coming.
expressions.example: There's a cold snap expected next week, so get your warm clothes ready.
It's bitterly cold today. It's too cold for my run.

expressions.phrase: How's the weather where you are?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about the weather in another place, e.g. on a call.
expressions.example: How's the weather where you are?

grammar.title: Weather words: noun, adjective, verb
grammar.explanation_ar: لكل كلمة طقس شكل اسم وصفة وأحيانًا فعل: rain → rainy → raining، snow → snowy → snowing، sun → sunny (والفعل: the sun is shining)، wind → windy، cloud → cloudy. بعد It is نستخدم الصفة أو الفعل بـ ing، وليس الاسم.
grammar.explanation_en: Weather words have noun, adjective and sometimes verb forms: rain → rainy → raining; snow → snowy → snowing; sun → sunny (verb: the sun is shining); wind → windy; cloud → cloudy. After "It is" use the adjective or the -ing verb, not the noun.
examples: It is rainy. / It is raining.
It is snowy. / It is snowing.
It is sunny. / The sun is shining.

grammar.title: It looks + adjective / It looks like + sentence
grammar.explanation_ar: It looks + صفة (It looks cold). It looks like + جملة (It looks like it's going to rain). تُستخدم لوصف ما نراه من النافذة.
grammar.explanation_en: Use "It looks + adjective" (It looks cold) or "It looks like + clause" (It looks like it's going to rain) to describe what you see.
examples: It looks a bit cold to me.
It looks like it's going to rain.
It looks settled for the weekend.

questions.question: How's the weather? — "It is ___."
questions.explanation_ar: بعد It is نستخدم snowing أو snowy، وليس الاسم snow.
questions.explanation_en: After "It is" use "snowing" or "snowy", not the noun "snow".

questions.question: A sudden, short burst of wind is a ___.
questions.explanation_en: A gust is a sudden burst of wind.

questions.question: Several days of very hot weather is a ___.
questions.explanation_en: A heatwave is several hot days.

questions.question: What is a "brolly"?
questions.explanation_ar: brolly كلمة بريطانية عامية تعني مظلة.

questions.question: Which is the opposite of a heatwave?
questions.explanation_ar: cold snap = موجة برد، عكس موجة الحر.
questions.explanation_en: A cold snap is the opposite of a heatwave.

questions.question: Look at those dark clouds. It looks ___ it's going to rain.
Why is the weather a good icebreaker?
choices: It is easy, safe and doesn't upset anyone.
questions.explanation_ar: الطقس موضوع سهل وآمن لا يزعج أحدًا.
questions.explanation_en: Weather is easy and safe; it doesn't upset anyone.
